title: Evercrest Analytics security & hosting intake
summary: Security intake to map Evercrest's requirements for PII handling, KMS integration, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs; evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options and compliance constraints (SOC2/ISO).
next_steps: Alex to share SOC2 and ISO certification matrix and security whitepaper by 2026-11-16
Priya to set up a 1-hour technical deep dive and live demo of Dedicated networking on 2026-11-20
Customer to provide data flow diagram and list of PII data types by 2026-11-18

transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-11-13
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Evercrest CTO), Sana Rao (Evercrest Head of Security), Leo Park (Evercrest Infra Architect)

Auto-Summary: Quick intake across compliance (SOC2/ISO), SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS, and audit log retention. Explored Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; customer leans toward private/dedicated for regulated workflows but wants clear tradeoffs and KMS controls.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Okay folks thanks for carving out time today really appreciate it. Quick round robin before we get into the details, Alex here from Redwood, Priya's our solutions engineer, over to Evercrest.
[00:12] Marcus Li: Hey Marcus li, CTO at Evercrest. We're running analytics on customer transaction data and a small amount of identifiable metadata. We're exploring how to safely host model inference for internal and some external features.
[00:22] Sana Rao: Sana Rao, Head of Security. I'm mostly here for compliance and KMS questions and to understand audit/log retention capabilities and exportability.
[00:30] Leo Park: Leo, infra architect. Interested in VPC setups, peering, and how Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private would map to our IaC patterns.

[00:45] Priya Kapoor: Great. Today's goals — map your compliance bar (SOC2/ISO), clarify SSO and SCIM for provisioning, KMS/customer-managed keys, where logs live, retention windows, and then recommend hosted/dedicated/private with tradeoffs. Sound good?
[00:58] Sana Rao: Yep that covers it. We have SOC2 Type II in flight and need to map vendor attestations. Also ISO 27001 is on the roadmap.

[01:10] Alex Chen: Quick question — are you wanting Redwood to hold keys for inference, or do you need customer-managed keys for decrypting model request payloads? I know this is a big hinge for private deployments.
[01:25] Marcus Li: Preference is customer-managed keys. Legal wants us to prove we control plaintext in production. So ideally our KMS — AWS KMS with external key policy, maybe CloudHSM for higher assurance. But open to options.
[01:39] Priya Kapoor: We support customer-managed keys in our Private offering and can integrate with AWS KMS via customer-managed CMKs. For Dedicated we also offer KMS passthrough where keys live in your account, but there are some constraints around egress for model cache snapshots. We'll outline those in the artifact we send.

[02:00] Sana Rao: On encryption, can you confirm disk encryption at rest for KV caches and any snapshots? Auditability around key rotation and access logs is critical.
[02:13] Priya Kapoor: Short answer: yes. Disk encryption with provider-managed volumes plus optional envelope encryption using your CMK. Rotation events and access by Redwood service principals are captured in CloudTrail inside your account when using customer-managed keys. We can also push audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[02:34] Leo Park: There was a note in your docs about cache snapshotting and model artifacts — where do those snapshots live and who can access them?
[02:45] Alex Chen: Snapshots for Dedicated live in the customer's VPC or a storage bucket in the customer's cloud account if you're using dedicated. For Hosted, snapshots are in Redwood-managed storage and cannot be stored in your account. For Private on-prem, snapshots remain on your infrastructure.

[03:05] Marcus Li: That makes sense. For SOC2, we need vendor-provided attestations and evidence of RBAC and separation of duties. How does Redwood present admin roles? We need to show auditors least privilege and admin logs.
[03:20] Priya Kapoor: We expose RBAC roles in the Console: Admin, Dev, Observability, and ReadOnly. These map to granular API scopes and team-level controls. All console and API admin actions produce audit entries; we retain them for X days by default, and enterprise customers can request extended retention exported to their S3 for 365/730 days depending on the plan.
[03:44] Sana Rao: What's the default retention 'X' you mentioned?
[03:47] Priya Kapoor: Defaults are 90 days for standard Hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private we typically configure 365 days or longer, exported to your storage to meet audit requirements.

[04:00] Alex Chen: Another question — what about SSO? Do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning?
[04:08] Priya Kapoor: Yes SAML 2.0 for login and SCIM v2 for user/group provisioning. We support IdPs like Okta and Azure AD. There are some nuances around provisioning for Dedicated where we can integrate with your SCIM endpoint inside the VPC.
[04:25] Leo Park: Any gotchas on SCIM tokens or provisioning frequency? We're trying to avoid long-lived tokens on our side.
[04:33] Priya Kapoor: SCIM tokens can be rotated and you can scope them to provisioning only. We recommend short TTLs and automated rotation if your IdP supports push-based rotation. We'll include recommended SCIM config in the follow-up doc.

[04:50] Marcus Li: Data residency — we have EU customer data and a requirement to keep logs in EU. Which hosting options guarantee regional data residency?
[05:00] Alex Chen: Hosted: we have EU regions and can pin workloads to them, but Hosted still uses Redwood-managed control plane which may route metadata through our control plane — we can document where metadata flows. Dedicated and Private give you stronger guarantees: Dedicated can be provisioned in your cloud region and Private keeps the control plane inside your VPC or on-prem.
[05:20] Sana Rao: We need explicit network diagrams and data flow for auditors showing where PII leaves our environment if at all.
[05:28] Priya Kapoor: Understood — we'll include an annotated data flow and a control-plane vs data-plane diagram. For Dedicated, data-plane stays in customer VPC when using private networking. Hosted will have control plane connections; we'll call out telemetry and metadata fields.

[05:45] Leo Park: How does model version pinning and rollouts look from a security/control perspective? We can't have a model changing behavior without approvals.
[05:55] Priya Kapoor: You can pin model versions per route. Rollouts are controlled via canary policies and require RBAC privileges to execute. We also have evaluation hooks and quality checks that can be gated in the pipeline so you can block automatic rollouts until manual sign-off.
[06:14] Marcus Li: Good. For legal we need indemnity language and contractual SLAs for data handling. What's typical in Redwood enterprise contracts?
[06:23] Alex Chen: We provide standard enterprise contract language with data processing addendum (DPA), indemnity clauses scaled to use, and SOC2/ISO attestation references. For Private deployments we can add stronger obligations around data residency and key handling.

[06:40] Sana Rao: Speaking of logs and forensic access: can Redwood provide raw request logs, or are those redacted in Hosted? We need the ability to investigate incidents internally.
[06:52] Priya Kapoor: In Hosted, raw request logs are redacted for customer PII by default; we provide structured telemetry and token-level cost metrics. For Dedicated/Private we can configure full request logging into your S3 with PII controls applied by your own tooling. We can also set up a redaction pipeline if you want us to handle redaction before logs leave the environment.
[07:20] Marcus Li: That redaction pipeline — is it run by Redwood or by us?
[07:25] Priya Kapoor: It can be either. For Dedicated we can optionally run a Redwood-managed redaction step inside your VPC under a service account you control. For Private you run everything.

[07:40] Alex Chen: Are there any regulatory constraints we should be aware of from your side — HIPAA, PCI, that sort of thing?
[07:46] Sana Rao: We're not processing full credit card numbers, but our customers include health-adjacent offerings so HIPAA could be relevant. We'll need BAA discussion if we handle PHI.
[07:58] Alex Chen: We do offer BAAs for certain enterprise plans, we'll flag legal to engage. Priya will include a checklist to determine if workload is PHI and next steps.

[08:10] Priya Kapoor: Quick note on pen testing and vulnerability management — Redwood runs quarterly pentests, monthly vulnerability scans, and has patch windows for runtime components. We can share the schedule and pen test summary redacted as part of the artifacts.
[08:26] Sana Rao: Do you provide CVE feeds and a timeline for remediation commitments?
[08:31] Priya Kapoor: Yes we publish a security bulletin and we commit to critical CVE remediation SLAs as per enterprise agreements. We'll include that in the security whitepaper.

[08:45] Leo Park: Networking — can we do private peering to Dedicated instances? We want to avoid NAT and public endpoints.
[08:53] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely. Dedicated supports VPC peering, PrivateLink equivalents, and cross-account roles for storage access. We'll provide sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets.

[09:05] Marcus Li: On cost tradeoffs, if we choose Dedicated plus CMK, what's the unit cost hit vs Hosted?
[09:12] Alex Chen: Generally Dedicated adds a fixed reserved capacity fee and slightly higher per-token compute costs due to reserved GPU pools. CMK integrations incur minimal infra cost but add ops overhead. We'll include rough delta estimates in the pricing packet.

[09:30] Sana Rao: We need a decision timeline. We're aiming to select a vendor and start a pilot by end of Q1 2027.
[09:37] Marcus Li: Yes pilot by March 2027. Initial scope: internal recommendations engine and a small external inference endpoint for partners.

[09:50] Priya Kapoor: Next steps recap: Alex will send SOC2/ISO artifact matrix and the security whitepaper, Priya will schedule a Dedicated networking deep-dive and attach SCIM/SSO config notes, Marcus will share a data flow diagram and PII inventory. Any other asks?
[10:08] Sana Rao: Also include BAA and PHI gating checklist.
[10:12] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll target the artifacts by Tuesday.

[10:25] Marcus Li: One last thing — are there references of similar regulated customers you can share? High level anonymized case studies?
[10:33] Alex Chen: Yes we have a couple, we'll pull anonymized references focusing on healthcare and payments customers. I'll include contact windows.

[10:45] Alex Chen: Cool thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and proposed times for the deep dive. Meeting ends.

End of transcript (approx transcription quality: medium — occasional mislabels and truncated words)
